Poetic licence
Poetry
Verse
items.s: Poetry is writing arranged in lines that uses rhythm and imagery to stir feeling.

items.q: “the reader's own feelings and views about a text” is the definition of
o: Personal response
Annotation
Literary appreciation
Re-reading
items.s: Personal response is the reader's own feelings and views about a text.

items.q: Three of these relate to African literature. Which one does not?
o: Oral tradition
African literature
Flashback
Praise singer
items.s: Every other option belongs to African literature. “Flashback” belongs to Narrative technique, not African literature.

items.q: “the matching of final sounds in words at the ends of lines” is the definition of
o: Poetry
Poetic licence
Line
Rhyme
items.s: Rhyme is the matching of final sounds in words at the ends of lines.

items.q: “a speech addressed to someone absent or to a thing” is the definition of
o: Alliteration
Apostrophe
Euphemism
Simile
items.s: Apostrophe is a speech addressed to someone absent or to a thing.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Chapter?
o: an account of a person's own life written by that person
a personal account of selected experiences rather than a whole life
a brief work of prose fiction built around a single incident or effect
a main division of a book that carries the story forward
items.s: Chapter: a main division of a book that carries the story forward. The other options describe Autobiography, Short story, Memoir.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Literary period.
o: the body of writing that a community inherits and continues to value
a category of literary work that shares form, subject matter and conventions
imaginative writing that uses language artfully to explore human experience and values
a span of years in which writers share styles and concerns
items.s: Literary period: a span of years in which writers share styles and concerns. The other options describe Genre, Literary tradition, Literature.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Rhyme.
o: a line of poetry or poetry considered as a whole
the regular or varied beat produced by stressed and light syllables
a single row of words in a poem, read as one unit
the matching of final sounds in words at the ends of lines
items.s: Rhyme: the matching of final sounds in words at the ends of lines. The other options describe Rhythm, Line, Verse.

items.q: In this course, Conflict refers to
o: the struggle between opposing forces that drives a story forward
the anxious uncertainty a reader feels about what happens next
an account of connected events told by a narrator
a hint early in a story about what will happen later
items.s: Conflict: the struggle between opposing forces that drives a story forward. The other options describe Foreshadowing, Suspense, Narrative.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Annotation?
o: notes written beside a text to mark points of interest
careful study of the exact words of a short passage
going through a text again to notice what was missed
the reader's own feelings and views about a text
items.s: Annotation: notes written beside a text to mark points of interest. The other options describe Close reading, Re-reading, Personal response.

items.q: Literary period may be defined as
o: the written work that a reader interprets and responds to
imaginative writing that uses language artfully to explore human experience and values
the treatment of literature as an art made out of words
a span of years in which writers share styles and concerns
items.s: Literary period: a span of years in which writers share styles and concerns. The other options describe Literature, Verbal art, Literary text.

items.q: The correct meaning of Metaphor is
o: a speech addressed to someone absent or to a thing
deliberate exaggeration used for emphasis rather than literal truth
a comparison that speaks of one thing as if it were another
the repetition of the same opening sound in nearby words
items.s: Metaphor: a comparison that speaks of one thing as if it were another. The other options describe Apostrophe, Hyperbole, Alliteration.

items.q: Interpretation may be defined as
o: the explanation of what a text means and how it means it
the informed enjoyment and understanding of a literary work
going through a text again to notice what was missed
notes written beside a text to mark points of interest
items.s: Interpretation: the explanation of what a text means and how it means it. The other options describe Annotation, Re-reading, Literary appreciation.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Rehearsal?
o: a short section of a play set in one place and time
the practice of a play before it is shown to an audience
a work written to be acted on a stage before an audience
the people who gather to watch and respond to a performance
items.s: Rehearsal: the practice of a play before it is shown to an audience. The other options describe Play, Scene, Audience.

items.q: “a comparison of two things using the words like or as” is the definition of
o: Simile
Personification
Onomatopoeia
Euphemism
items.s: Simile is a comparison of two things using the words like or as.

items.q: “the use of words whose sound suggests the thing they name” is the definition of
o: Onomatopoeia
Oxymoron
Hyperbole
Apostrophe
items.s: Onomatopoeia is the use of words whose sound suggests the thing they name.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a traditional story about a real place or person, much embellished”
o: Legend
African literature
Call and response
Work song
items.s: Legend is a traditional story about a real place or person, much embellished.

items.q: “the struggle between opposing forces that drives a story forward” is the definition of
o: Flashback
Theme
Climax
Conflict
items.s: Conflict is the struggle between opposing forces that drives a story forward.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “an account of a person's own life written by that person”
o: Memoir
Prose fiction
Prose
Autobiography
items.s: Autobiography is an account of a person's own life written by that person.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Review.
o: a reasoned judgement of the strengths and weaknesses of a text
the conclusion a reader reaches about the worth of a work
a leaning towards one side that distorts fair judgement
a short published assessment of a book written for readers
items.s: Review: a short published assessment of a book written for readers. The other options describe Judgement, Bias, Critique.

items.q: The correct meaning of Verse is
o: a line of poetry or poetry considered as a whole
the freedom a poet takes to depart from ordinary grammar and fact
a single row of words in a poem, read as one unit
the person who composes a poem and shapes its language
items.s: Verse: a line of poetry or poetry considered as a whole. The other options describe Line, Poet, Poetic licence.

items.q: The correct meaning of Play is
o: a work written to be acted on a stage before an audience
the written text of a play with its words and directions
the practice of a play before it is shown to an audience
the group of actors who perform the roles in a play
items.s: Play: a work written to be acted on a stage before an audience. The other options describe Cast, Script, Rehearsal.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Bias.
o: words and passages from the text used to support a claim
a leaning towards one side that distorts fair judgement
the conclusion a reader reaches about the worth of a work
a short published assessment of a book written for readers
items.s: Bias: a leaning towards one side that distorts fair judgement. The other options describe Review, Textual evidence, Judgement.

items.q: In this course, Narrator refers to
o: the voice that tells the story in a work of fiction
a hint early in a story about what will happen later
the anxious uncertainty a reader feels about what happens next
an account of connected events told by a narrator
items.s: Narrator: the voice that tells the story in a work of fiction. The other options describe Foreshadowing, Narrative, Suspense.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Apostrophe.
o: a comparison that speaks of one thing as if it were another
a phrase that joins two words with opposite meanings
deliberate exaggeration used for emphasis rather than literal truth
a speech addressed to someone absent or to a thing
items.s: Apostrophe: a speech addressed to someone absent or to a thing. The other options describe Hyperbole, Metaphor, Oxymoron.
